title: Attach sampled request/response frames to routing decision logs for faster RCA
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: When smart routing makes region/tier/model-variant decisions we capture a decision record, but engineers often need the minimal surrounding request/response ‘frames’ to debug regressions or quality issues. Today we store long traces or full payloads only for manually-triggered playbacks which is slow and expensive to query. This ticket proposes attaching compact, sampled request/response frames to decision logs to make RCA faster while bounding cost and privacy risk.

Goals: 1) enable sub-second root cause analysis for routing-related errors and quality regressions; 2) keep per-decision telemetry small (<= 1KB average) and cost predictable; 3) respect PII policy and opt-out controls; 4) allow adaptive sampling by error type, customer tier, and region.
proposed_solution:
- For a subset of routing decisions (configurable sampling policy) capture a compact frame bundle containing: request metadata (route id, model variant, region, tier, token counts), a redacted prompt prefix up to 512 bytes, the first 128 bytes of the model response and any fallback reason codes.
- Store frame bundles as compressed, base64-encoded blobs in the decision-log store with a per-frame size cap (e.g., 2KB). The decision record will include a small pointer (frame_id) and inline summary fields for fast queries.
- Sampling policy: default 0.1% of successful decisions, 5% of decisions with latency > SLO, and 100% of decisions with error class >= RetryableError or QualityRegression events. Policies are overridable by project/tier.
- Privacy: apply server-side PII redaction pipeline before storing frames (token filter + name/email regex + configurable customer allowlist). For Private deployments, frames can be omitted or routed to customer-owned blob storage.
- Query surface: extend decision logs API with ?include_frames=true and a time-bucketed frame lookup endpoint (fast cache layer for last 7 days).
- Backwards compatibility: if frame storage is disabled, decision records remain unchanged and contain an empty frame_id.
design_notes: Frame format v1: {version, frame_id, timestamp, route_meta, redacted_prompt_snippet, response_snippet, fallback_code, compressed_blob_size}
Store compressed blobs in s3-like object store with lifecycle policy (30d hot, 90d cold, then delete) and warm cache in redis for 7d.
Use adaptive sampling rules implemented in the routing decision service so we capture frames at the point of decision with minimal extra RPCs.
Trade-offs: storing full payloads would make debugging easier but increases cost and PII risk. Compact snippets strike a balance for most RCA cases.
We evaluated alternatives: (a) capture full KV cache snapshots (too large), (b) rely on existing trace context and re-run requests (slow/expensive).
implementation_plan: 1) Add a frame builder in router: generate compact snippets and apply redaction (owner: Lena) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/748
2) Frame store shim: implement put/get to object store + redis cache (owner: SRE - Ravi) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/frame-store/pull/29
3) Decision-log schema migration: add frame_id field and inline summary columns (owner: Marco) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/decision-log/pull/103
4) API surface: new query param include_frames and frame lookup endpoint (owner: API team) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/api/pull/421
5) E2E tests + sampling config UI in Console (owner: QA/UX) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/88
acceptance_criteria: Given default sampling, we observe <=1KB average per stored frame bundle and cost projection for 30d under normal traffic
Frames contain redacted prompt snippet and response snippet with no high-confidence PII (verified by automated scanner)
Engineers can retrieve frames via decision logs API and find context to resolve at least 70% of routing incidents in staging playbacks
Feature toggle exists to disable frame storage per tenant and in Private deployments
Unit+integration tests cover sampling policy boundary conditions and storage lifecycle
test_plan: - Unit tests for redaction pipeline and snippet truncation; integration test wiring router -> frame-store -> decision-log; load test sampling path at 10x production to validate performance; privacy test that runs known PII strings through redaction and asserts removal. Create a staging dashboard with synthetic incidents to validate retrieval latency < 200ms for cached frames and < 1s for cold lookups.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable frames for 100% of sampling conditions but only store in staging bucket. Monitor size and redaction failures (1 week).
Phase 2 (canary): enable 1% production traffic for non-sensitive tiers and a single region. Validate cost and privacy guards (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (regional ramp): increase sampling to target rates across regions with SLO for frame storage latency; enable Console toggle for projects (3 weeks).
Phase 4: full GA with lifecycle policy and documentation updates
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — built prototype frame builder in router that emits compressed snippets. Verified 0.6KB avg size on sampled traffic.
2026-03-04: Security reviewed prototype redaction approach; requested regex hardening and add names/email heuristic. Assigned to Marco to add tests.
2026-03-06: Frame-store shim initial implementation merged to feature branch. Redis cache working for last-7d hot lookups.
2026-03-08: Discovered edge-case: responses with binary attachments inflate blob size. Added rule to drop binary payloads and log a metric. Blocking note — need policy decision for attachments.
2026-03-10: Decided to exclude attachments and only capture textual outputs; continuing API and decision-log migration. On track for staging spike next week.
